key_idea: Factor n−θ in the number field as α^kβ with conjugates of α and β balanced, then pair small boxes of their projective directions and apply bihomogeneous determinant cuts on the resulting bicone. This feeds a general affine counting theorem that uses adaptive auxiliary primes and random deletion.
reason: The algebraic factorization α^kβ=μ(n−θ) is a striking idea. It turns the large-prime tail into a determinant-method count on a bicone, but it is buried under paired-box bookkeeping, lattice reductions, Hilbert-function estimates, quartic-specific geometry (including the quintic critical-value family), and an exact finite parameter certificate. The sieve transfer is clean and standard, but the main estimate is a long chain of lemmas whose numerical thresholds come from a case-by-case parameter search rather than one transparent reason.
